newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechinvest confirms Toray plant decision.
newsitem.headline: Czechinvest confirms Toray plant decision.

text.p: The state investment support agency Czechinvest said on Thursday that Japan's Toray Industries Inc. has decided to build a polyester weaving and dyeing plant in the eastern Czech city of Prostejov.
In a statement, Czechinvest said that the greenfield project would consist of fully-automated weaving and dying lines for polyster linings.

"Operated to the highest technical and environmental standards, the plant will introduce a series of management practices and innovations new to the Czech textiles industry that are modelled on a similar successful Toray plant in the (United Kingdom)," Czechinvest said.
The Toray Textiles Europe Ltd (TTEL) plant, in the English city of Mansfield, was completed in 1994 with investment of $150 million.
It said the Czech Toray plant would be regarded as the second TTEL plant.

A specific investment figure planned for the Czech plant was not disclosed. The Czech agency CTK quoted Czechinvest director Jan Havelka as saying that Toray's investment target for the Prostejov plant was at about $150 million.

"Setting up a production site in the Czech Republic will strengthen our firm's position in Europe and allow us entry to the markets of CEFTA (the Central European Free Trade Agreement)," Toray's president Katsunosuke Maeda was quoted as saying in the Czechinvest statement.
CEFTA consists of Poland, Hungary, Slovenia, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic.
Czechinvest said the purchase procedure for 240,000 square metres of land -- in Prostejov where the Czech textile industry is concentrated -- has begun and should be completed by the middle of 1997.
There was no comment on when the plant would begin operation.
